parts:
Progress so far on the N4SYM first session (derivations done and both check programs written and passing; the note is up next):

- **Quadratic shape response is fully fixed by B.** log Z = πB∫(|k|³|ĥ|² − |k||ĵ|²) + c_R∫ḣ² + O(ε⁴). The perimeter constant c_R is the only thing a scheme can change. The Zarembo profile j = ḣ cancels exactly, and that cancellation is equivalent to C_D = 6C_Φ.
- **The linear retarded response of the straight line is local.** χ_R(ω) = m_Rω² + 2πiBω³, which is Abraham–Lorentz radiation reaction. The cause is Huygens' principle together with the protected Δ = 2. The total work is 2πB‖ḧ‖², which matches CHMS exactly. But the renormalized finite-time account is negative at the onset of every drive, whatever the finite mass. The spectral cutoff model stays passive only because of its mass term δm = 4BΛ. So the straight-line linear channel cannot carry the arithmetic transfer: it has no memory, no variable exponent and no delays.
- **The proposal's first growing-trace observable is a poor choice.** That observable is the trace plus a straight chord with constant n₀. It forms a thin sliver whose value blows up like exp(κ/(a√t)). The a = 0 case is infinite, so it cannot serve as a control. The tangent-coupled alternative is trivial, since ⟨W⟩ = 1 (Zarembo).
- **Recommended replacement: flip the scalar direction on the return chord.** This restores the a = 0 identity control. I derived its exact first evolution equation and checked it by finite differences on a noncommuting background.

parts:
I've analyzed the flipped-return loop (scalar direction n₀ on the trace, −n₀ on the return chord), and it holds up: it is finite and well behaved in every regime I checked. Its leading dependence on s = a√t comes from the shape of the curve rather than its perimeter. Nothing in it resembles the shifted-zeta transfer, so no arithmetic comparison is warranted yet.

**What I found about the flipped-return loop**
- **Exact evolution equations.** The first two evolution equations are exact for smooth fields and hold for any driver with a C² trace. Both match finite differences on a noncommuting SU(2) test background.
  - The coefficient of the scalar insertion at the tip is exactly the rate at which trace length minus chord length grows. That is why this family measures shape while the constant-n₀ version measured perimeter.
- **Short-time law at fixed flow smoothing.** The formula W = 1 + O(a²t³) was confirmed term by term by a separate one-loop flowed calculation.
- **One loop, no smoothing.** With small neighbourhoods of the two cusps cut out, W ≈ 1 − (2πB₁/3)|s|(log(ℓ/ε) − 2). The coefficient of the logarithm is exactly the one-loop cusp value, and the constant term matches the predicted 4π/3 to about 10⁻⁴.
- **Three regimes with flow smoothing.**
  - When the smoothing scale is much larger than the loop, W − 1 grows like a²t³.
  - In an intermediate band it goes like s²√(t/τ).
  - When the smoothing scale is smallest, it goes like |s|·log|s|.
  - None diverges. The extra log|s| is a scheme effect at nearly supersymmetric cusps.
- **Not closed.** The second equation brings in terms the field equations don't remove: derivatives transverse to the plane, ordered pairs of insertions, and a scalar gradient at the tip.
- **Open question.** The all-orders coefficient of the |s|·log term is not known beyond one loop. The standard near-BPS cusp formula doesn't apply in this corner; at one loop it is off by a factor of 2.

**Corrections to the first note.** A separate reviewer instance confirmed all the core coefficients but found errors in the surrounding text, now fixed:
- The locality of the straight-line response comes from one-dimensional conformal symmetry and the displacement's integer dimension, in any bulk dimension. I had wrongly attributed it to Huygens' principle.
- The finite-time energy account is negative after every drive whose onset has finite order. It is not negative for every smooth drive: an oscillating onset is a counterexample.
- One proof step, one hypothesis and one sign in the transfer function were wrong.

**Checks run.** There are three check programs, all standard library only, with 72, 77 and 47 cases. All pass on your machine, give identical output on repeated runs, and have saved records. Nothing has been reviewed by an independent specialist.

**Next steps.** The continuation note gives the order of work. The cheapest step is to take the published two-loop and strong-coupling cusp formula (Drukker–Forini) and read off that open coefficient.

**Things you need to do.**
- **Stale git lock.** A `git status` I ran left an empty stale file, `.git/index.lock`, which I couldn't delete. Remove it before your next `git add`.
- **Package check.** `validation/check_package.py check` was already failing at the proposal commit `8b22141`, and my new files add more mismatches. I didn't run `refresh`, because it overwrites the hand-written author and scope fields in the package record.
- **Not committed.** Nothing from this session is committed.

I also replaced the project's next-session prompt with the N4SYM handoff; the old fractional-dimension prompt is still in the repo.

parts:
I finished all three next steps. The main result: the open coefficient H is one-loop exact in the limit s → 0, but how quickly that limit is reached depends on an effective coupling g = λ|s|. At strong coupling a new √(λ|s|) regime appears. A separate reviewer instance re-derived everything below with its own code and confirmed it; its six scope and wording corrections are applied.

**1. The coefficient H**
- **An exact anchor.** A published exact near-BPS formula (Correa–Henn–Maldacena–Sever) fixes, at every coupling, the slope of the cusp exactly at the BPS line. In the corner relevant to the flipped loop (deflection near π, internal angle π), that slope depends only on g = λu.
- **Two loops.** I used the published two-loop cusp (Drukker–Forini), after checking it against three independent limits. Through two loops the corner is (1 − x²)[g/16π − g²/192π²]. So H = λ(1 − 1/N²)/16π, with no two-loop correction.
- **All orders.** H stays at its one-loop value order by order in perturbation theory. This rests on a standard but unproven bound on the antiparallel-lines limit.
- **Strong coupling.** I derived the classical-string corner in closed parametric form: Γ = √(λu)·F(x), with F(0) ≈ 0.1750. It reproduces the exact slope at the BPS line, which is a strong consistency check.
  - The string reaches much deeper than the cusp is wide (depth ~√u), which is where the √(λu) behaviour comes from.
  - A by-product: near internal angle π, the strong-coupling potential between antiparallel lines goes like (π − θ)^{3/2}, where weak coupling gives (π − θ)². I didn't find this in the literature, but it may be known.
- **What this means for the flipped loop.** The effective coupling is g(t) = λ|a|√t/3, so Loewner time sets it. The short-time law is one-loop-like at small t. At strong coupling it becomes about 0.20·√(λ|s|)·log once t passes roughly 9/(λa)².

**2. Rounded family.** Replacing each cusp by a circular arc of radius δ gives a finite one-loop result.
- The coefficient of log(1/δ) is exactly the one-loop cusp sum, as it must be.
- The constant term depends on the rounding convention: h = −4.0202, and the reviewer's independent code gave −4.02025.
- The |s| log|s| term comes from where the arc touches the legs, about 6δ/|s| from the corner. Every regulator that acts on the distance between points gives the same term.

**3. Closure audit.** The field equations reduce only part of the second evolution equation, so the flipped hierarchy is not closed.
- What survives:
  - the transverse gauge currents and the transverse scalar Laplacian;
  - scalar and fermion currents;
  - scalar-potential and Yukawa insertions;
  - scalar commutators from transport along the chord;
  - the scalar gradient at the tip;
  - ordered pairs of insertions.
- Already at one loop, the field-equation part is a pure regulator contact term, while the transverse part has a long-range 4/r⁴ kernel. So the leftover terms can't be dropped even in perturbation theory.

**Checks.** Two new check programs (56 and 20 cases), standard library only. Across the investigation there are now five programs and 272 cases, all passing and reproducible on your machine.

**Direction.** The flipped-loop physics is in good shape. The link to the Weil form hasn't strengthened, though: these are Euclidean expectation values with no input/output channel. The continuation note therefore offers two paths:
- (A) Finish the flipped family as a standalone physics result: three-loop corner, then a quantum correction to the string corner.
- (B) Go back to the arithmetic goal and look for a channel with memory, most concretely the response of a finite-mass quark (string endpoint).

Which would you like next?

**Housekeeping.**
- The stale `.git/index.lock` from last time is gone.
- You seem to have renamed the parent's `DRAFT_HISTOR.md` to `DRAFT_HISTORY.md`, so I repointed the dangling link in the wilson-loewner README. The WZW copy still has the old name.
- Nothing is committed.
- I replaced the project's next-session prompt with the new handoff.

Files are in `wilson-loewner/N4SYM`:
- notes/NEAR_BPS_CORNER_ROUNDING_AND_CLOSURE_20260924.md
- notes/CONTINUATION_AFTER_SECOND_SESSION_20260924.md
- reviews/review_claude_second_session_20260924.md
- numerics/check_near_bps_corner.py
- numerics/check_rounded_and_closure.py

Sources:
- [Drukker–Forini, arXiv:1105.5144](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.5144) (formulas read through an automated summary, then checked against three limits)
- [Correa–Henn–Maldacena–Sever, arXiv:1202.4455](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.4455)
- [Gromov–Levkovich-Maslyuk, arXiv:1601.05679](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.05679) (searched for the (π − θ)^{3/2} law; not found)

archive_metadata.source_kind: Claude Cowork cloud session event log (claude.ai GET /v1/code/sessions/{id}/events), read in the signed-in browser and reduced to completed public messages
archive_metadata.message_timestamps: Event times, in seconds since Unix epoch and ISO 8601: the session's own timestamp where the event carries one, otherwise the server's event time (typed messages); the conversation create_time is the session's creation time in the session list
archive_metadata.coverage: Messages typed by the person (including any sent while a reply was in progress, with the names of files sent with them) and interruption markers; the options the person selected in question cards; the assistant text shown in the chat: progress lines between tool calls, question cards rendered as text, notes and file-card captions sent through tools (phase commentary), and the text ending each completed turn (phase final_answer); recorded through the event log as read
omitted_record_types: system, developer and harness text (reminders, date notes, memory snapshots, continuation summaries, hook feedback, skill text, local command output)
tool calls and outputs, except the chat-visible items named in coverage
permission prompts, control and environment events, usage and cost figures
attachment contents (file names are kept in message metadata)
